summary: The scene protocols Stettler's written confession and Rieder's formal acceptance of it with dry, bureaucratic precision and earns its place through fact-arranged irony (the frozen-man aphorism, Rieder's steady signature against Stettler's tremor); one line breaks that discipline by having the narrator gloss the moment's future significance instead of just showing it.
